summary: Build stronger business decisions with SWOT, 5 Whys, and decision matrices. Train your team to analyze, compare, and justify actions.
lede: Analytical thinking for business decisions gives you a structured way to define problems, assess evidence, identify root causes, and compare realistic options. You will practise using SWOT analysis, Pareto analysis, the 5 Whys, and decision matrices to turn incomplete information and competing views into focused recommendations. The course helps you document assumptions, test hypotheses, rank alternatives, and write concise decision briefs that managers and executives can act on. You will also explore how AI-assisted summaries and spreadsheet-based analysis can support evidence review while applying methods you can use in meetings, reporting cycles, and project reviews.
audienceIntro: This course is designed for professionals who must diagnose business issues, compare options, and justify decisions with evidence.
prerequisites: To get the most from this course, you should have working experience in a business, operations, finance, project, or analyst role and comfort reading basic reports and spreadsheets. No coding is required. Familiarity with Microsoft Excel, internal performance reports, or KPI dashboards will help you complete the exercises more confidently. This is an intermediate-level course, so you should already be able to describe your team's problems and data sources, but you do not need prior formal training in analytical frameworks.
